words.gram: f. inst. sg. (form and sense uncertain)

hindi: किस सहायता से अद्भुत, सदा बढ़ने वाला मित्र हमारे पास आएगा? किस सबसे शक्तिशाली से?
english: By what help will the wondrous, ever-increasing friend come to us? By what most powerful [unclear]?
notes: ā bhuvat is read as 'will come to be (with us)'; naḥ may be 'to us' or 'our'. sadāvṛdhaḥ 'ever-increasing' may also be 'ever-strengthening (us)'. The last word vṛtā (instrumental of an uncertain noun, perhaps 'band' or 'course') is left as [unclear] in English and omitted in Hindi; śaciṣṭhayā is then left without a noun.

hindi: कौन सत्य, मदों में सबसे उदार, रस से तुम्हें आनन्दित करेगा? दृढ़ वस्तुओं को भी तोड़ने के लिए धन।
english: Which true one, the most bountiful of the exhilarations, will gladden you with the juice? To break open even firm things: wealth.
notes: The '~' in ma~hiṣṭho is the candrabindu for anusvāra (maṃhiṣṭha). vasu is taken as neuter 'wealth' standing loosely after āruje; it could also be a vocative 'O good one' (vaso would then be expected). andhasaḥ (genitive/ablative) is rendered 'with the juice'; the grammar of the second line is loose and no verb is supplied.

words.gram: pron. 1 pl. acc./gen./dat. (naḥ, retroflex after ṣu)
n. acc. sg. used as adv.

hindi: हमारे प्रति भली प्रकार मित्रों और स्तोताओं के सहायक बनो, सौ गुना होकर सहायता के लिए।
english: Be a good helper toward us, of friends, of singers; be a hundredfold, for help.
notes: abhī is abhi with Vedic lengthening; ṇaḥ is naḥ with retroflex n after ṣu. jaritṝṇām is the Vedic genitive plural of jaritṛ. śatam is read as adverbial 'hundredfold'; the text does not say what is hundredfold. Whether abhi goes with bhavāsi ('overcome') or is a plain 'toward us' is not settled.

words.gram: pres. part. mid. √mand, m. acc. sg.

hindi: उस को, तुम्हारे लिए, अद्भुत, आक्रमणों को जीतने वाले, धन और रस में आनन्दित होने वाले को; जैसे बाड़ों में गौएँ बछड़े की ओर, वैसे हम इन्द्र की ओर स्तुतियों से ऊँचे स्वर से पुकारते हैं।
english: Him, for you, the marvellous one, overcomer of onsets, rejoicing in wealth and in the juice: as milch cows call out loudly to the calf in the stalls, so we call out loudly to Indra with songs.
notes: vaḥ is rendered 'for you' (it could also be 'your'). vasoḥ and andhasaḥ are both taken as genitives after mandānam ('rejoicing in wealth, in the juice'); vasoḥ could instead be 'of the good one'. ṛtīṣaham 'overcoming onsets' is kept whole. navāmahe is rendered 'we call out loudly' for both the cows and the singers; the cows' verb is the same verb in the text.

words.gram: m. acc. sg. (sense of kṣu uncertain)

hindi: हम शीघ्र दीप्तिमान, उत्तम दाता को, जो शक्तियों से घिरा है, जो पर्वत के समान अनेक भोगों वाला है, और प्रचुर वाज को, जो सैकड़ों वाला, हज़ारों वाला, गायों से भरपूर है, माँगते हैं।
english: We quickly seek the radiant one, the good giver, surrounded by powers, of many enjoyments like a mountain, and the abounding prize, with hundreds, with thousands, rich in cattle.
notes: The '~' in dyukṣa~, vāja~, śatina~ is the candrabindu for anusvāra (-m). The first accusatives (dyukṣam, sudānum, āvṛtam, purubhojasam) name no god; the text gives no noun, so none is supplied. 'like a mountain' may qualify the giver or the enjoyments. kṣumantam (from kṣu) is rendered 'abounding'; its exact sense is uncertain. The verb īmahe is rendered 'we seek' (it can be 'implore').

words.gram: m. acc. sg., compound (pres. part. √vid + vasu)
n. acc. sg. used as adv.

hindi: तुम्हारे लिए, तीव्र शक्तियों के साथ, संकट में पड़े हुए हम धन पाने वाले इन्द्र को सहायता के लिए बुलाते हैं; सोम निचोड़े जाने वाले यज्ञ में ऊँचे स्वर से गाते हुए मैं बुलाता हूँ, जैसे संघर्ष के लिए कर्ता को।
english: For you, with swift powers, we, hard-pressed, [call] Indra, the finder of wealth, for help; singing loudly at the rite where Soma is pressed, I call, like a doer for the fray.
notes: The first line has no verb; 'call' is supplied from huve. The plural sabādhaḥ and gāyantaḥ go with 'we', but huve is singular ('I'). vaḥ may be 'your'. bṛhat is rendered 'loudly' (literally 'greatly'). bharam is 'fray' (also 'burden'); the simile 'bharaṃ na kāriṇam' is obscure and kept literal.

words.gram: pf. part. mid. √śam, m. dat. sg.

hindi: जिसे न प्रचण्ड और न दृढ़ रोक पाते हैं, रस के मदों में; जो आदर करके परिश्रम करने वाले, निचोड़ने वाले स्तोता को प्रशंसनीय का दाता है।
english: Whom neither the fierce nor the firm hold back [unclear] in the exhilarations of the juice [unclear]; who, having honoured, is the giver of what is praiseworthy to the toiling one who presses, to the singer.
notes: Two words are unclear: muro (perhaps muraḥ, 'obstructing', or a corruption) and śipram (perhaps 'lip, jaw, helmet' or an epithet); both are left as [unclear] in English and omitted in Hindi, and no firm sentence can be built on the first half. dudhrāḥ is taken as 'fierce'. śaśamānāya may mean 'toiling' or 'praising'. ukthyam has no noun; 'what is' is supplied. jaritra = jaritre before u-.

hindi: हे सोम, सबसे स्वादिष्ट, सबसे मादक धारा से छनकर बहो; इन्द्र के पीने के लिए निचोड़े हुए।
english: Flow clear, O Soma, with the sweetest, most exhilarating stream, pressed for Indra to drink.

hindi: राक्षसों का संहारक, सब लोगों का, स्थान की ओर, लौह से आहत में, द्रोण में, साझे आसन पर बैठा।
english: The slayer of Rakṣas, of all peoples, sat down toward the seat, in the iron-struck [one], in the trough, on the common seat.
notes: viśvacarṣaṇiḥ is taken as 'of all peoples' (carṣaṇi = peoples); 'all-seeing' is possible. ayohate (loc. of ayas + hata, 'struck/worked with iron') has no noun; 'one' is supplied in English and the word is left without a noun in Hindi. The subject is not named; 'he' comes from the verb ending.

words.gram: m. nom. sg., tat-puruṣa (varivas + dhā, superl.)

hindi: तुम विस्तृत स्थान देने वालों में श्रेष्ठतम, सबसे उदार, वृत्र के सर्वश्रेष्ठ संहारक बनते हो; तुम उदारों की उदारता को पूर्ण करते हो।
english: You become the best bestower of room, the most bountiful, the best slayer of Vṛtra; you bring to fulfilment the bounty of the bountiful ones.
notes: The addressee is not named. The '~' in ma~hiṣṭho is the candrabindu for anusvāra. parṣi 'bring to fulfilment' (also 'carry across').

words.gram: m. nom. sg., tat-puruṣa (kratu + vid, superl.)
n. acc. sg. used as adv.

hindi: हे सबसे मधुर, इन्द्र के लिए छनकर बहो, हे सोम; शक्ति के सर्वश्रेष्ठ खोजी, मद; अत्यन्त सबसे दीप्तिमान, मद।
english: Flow clear, O sweetest, for Indra, O Soma; the best finder of power, the exhilaration; greatly the most radiant, the exhilaration.
notes: mahi is taken as an adverb ('greatly'); as the neuter of mahā 'great' it does not agree with the masculine madaḥ. kratu = power. Both nominatives are in apposition to the addressee.

hindi: तुम्हारे जिसको पीकर बैल बैल की तरह आचरण करता है, इस प्रकाश पाने वाले को पीकर वह सुस्पष्ट दिखने वाला पोषण की ओर, वाज की ओर बढ़ा, एतश के समान।
english: Having drunk of that of yours, the bull acts like a bull; having drunk of this light-finding one, he, the clearly seen, strode toward the refreshments, toward the prize, like Etaśa.
notes: The drink is not named; yasya and asya refer to it and svarvidaḥ (genitive of svar-vid, 'light-finding') is taken with asya. The subject of akramīt is 'he' (sa), probably the same as the bull; this is not stated. etaśa is a steed or the name Etaśa; kept as 'Etaśa' with na 'like'. iṣaḥ is the accusative plural 'refreshments' (genitive singular 'of refreshment' is possible).

words.gram: pp. √su, m. nom. pl. (visarga lost before i-)

hindi: इन्द्र की ओर, बलवान की ओर, ये निचोड़े हुए भूरे जाएँ; शीघ्र जन्मी हुई बूँदें, सूर्य का प्रकाश पाने वाली।
english: Toward Indra, the mighty one, let these pressed ones go, the tawny ones; the drops born readily, finders of the light of heaven.
notes: sutāḥ and harayaḥ are read as the same pressed drops; the text names no noun for them. śruṣṭe is rendered 'readily' (also 'quickly'). svar = light of heaven.

hindi: यह विजयी, निचोड़ा हुआ, संघर्ष के लिए इन्द्र हेतु छनकर बहता है; सोम विजय का ध्यान रखता है, जैसा वह जानता है।
english: This winning one, pressed, flows clear for Indra, for the fray; Soma is mindful of victory, as he knows.
notes: cetati with a genitive is taken as 'is mindful of'; the lexicon sense 'is perceived, shines' (with jaitrasya as a qualifier) is possible. vide is 3 sg. perfect middle 'he knows'; 'is known' is possible (so taken in 645). bharāya 'for the fray' (also 'for bearing').

hindi: इसके मदों में इन्द्र ही जीतने वाली पकड़ को पकड़ता है, और जलों में विजयी ने बलवान वज्र को एकत्र किया।
english: Indra indeed, in the exhilarations of this one, seizes the winning grasp, and, winner in the waters, brought together the mighty thunderbolt.
notes: 'this one' (asya) is not named. grābha 'grasp, handful'. The present gṛbhṇāti and the past bharat are as in the text. sam bharat is taken as 'brought together' (also 'gathered, wielded').

hindi: तुम्हारे रस के प्रथम विजय में, निचोड़े हुए, मदकारी के लिए; हे मित्रो, लम्बी जीभ वाले कुत्ते को दूर मारो।
english: In the foremost victory of your juice, for the pressed, exhilarating one: strike away the dog, O friends, the long-tongued one.
notes: The first line has no verb; it is read as a loose phrase leading to the command. 'the pressed, exhilarating one' has no noun. The '~' in śvāna~ is the candrabindu for anusvāra.

hindi: जो निचोड़ा हुआ पवित्र करने वाली धारा से चारों ओर बहता है, वह बूँद प्रभावशाली घोड़े के समान है।
english: He who, pressed, flows all around with the purifying stream is the drop, like an effective steed.
notes: The sentence has no main verb; 'is' is supplied in both languages. indu = drop.

hindi: उस सोम की ओर, हे मनुष्यो, सर्वव्यापी बुद्धि से; यज्ञ के लिए पत्थर हों।
english: Toward him, the [unclear] Soma, O men, with all-pervading thought; for the sacrifice let the stones be.
notes: duroṣa (perhaps 'hard to burn/consume' or 'unharmed') is uncertain, left as [unclear] in English and omitted in Hindi. naraḥ may be a nominative ('the men') rather than a vocative. abhī is abhi with Vedic lengthening. The relation of santu to the first line (an abhi-verb may be lost) is unclear.

hindi: प्रसन्नता में स्थित वह प्रिय नामों की ओर छनकर बहता है, जिनमें वह ओजस्वी बढ़ता है; महान सूर्य के सर्वतोमुख रथ पर महान सर्वद्रष्टा आरूढ़ हुआ।
english: Set in delight, he flows clear toward the dear names, in which the vigorous one grows; the all-seeing, great one mounted upon the all-turning chariot of the great sun.
notes: canohito = canaḥ-hitaḥ ('set in delight'; cana = delight or food). viṣvañcam 'all-turning' (also 'moving everywhere'); bṛhann adhi is read 'great, upon' with the chariot. The subject is not named.

hindi: ऋत की जिह्वा मधुर, प्रिय बहती है; वक्ता, इस बुद्धि का स्वामी, अहिंसित। पुत्र दोनों माता-पिता के छिपे तीसरे नाम को आकाश के दीप्तिमान लोक पर स्थापित करता है।
english: The tongue of truth flows clear, sweet, dear; the speaker, the lord of this thought, the unharmed one. The son sets the hidden third name of the two parents upon the luminous realm of heaven.
notes: madhu priyam is read as the adjectives 'sweet, dear' used loosely after pavate (it could be 'the dear sweet [stream]'). pitroḥ is the dual 'of the two parents'; whose parents is not stated. apīcyā3ṃ is apīcyam with the pluta mark 3 (a separate chant word, not translated). adābhya 'unharmed' (also 'not to be deceived').

words.gram: pres. part. mid. √dyut, m. nom. sg.
pres. part. pass. √yam, m. nom. sg.

hindi: चमकता हुआ वह कलशों पर गरजा, मनुष्यों से नियन्त्रित, सुनहरे कोश में। ऋत के दोहन की ओर गूँजे हैं; उषा के तीन पीठ वाले स्थान पर तुम चमकते हो।
english: Shining, he roared down at the vessels, held by men in the golden vat. The milkings of truth have resounded toward; upon the three-ridged [height] of Dawn you shine forth.
notes: The '~' in kalaśā~ is the candrabindu for anusvāra (kalaśān). 'abhī' is abhi with Vedic lengthening; abhi anūṣata has no object, so it is rendered 'resounded toward'. The shift from 'he' (line 1) to 'you' (rājasi) is as in the text. tripṛṣṭhe uṣasaḥ is read 'on the three-ridged [height] of Dawn' ('height' is supplied in English only); uṣasaḥ may instead be an accusative plural ('over the Dawns'). kośa is kośe before ā.

hindi: हर यज्ञ में तुम्हारे लिए अग्नि को, और हर स्तुति से कुशल को: हम आगे बढ़कर अमर जातवेदा की स्तुति करें, जो प्रिय है, मित्र के समान।
english: At every sacrifice, for you, to Agni, and with every song, to the skilful one: we would proclaim forth the immortal Jātavedas, dear, like Mitra.
notes: śaṃsiṣam is 1 sg. in form while the subject vayam is plural; rendered 'we would proclaim'. mitram na is 'like Mitra' (glossary); 'like a friend' is possible. The '~' in śa~siṣam is the candrabindu for anusvāra. The cases of yajñāyajñā and girāgirā (distributive repetition) are taken as locative and instrumental.

hindi: हम बल के पुत्र की सेवा करें, हव्य देने के लिए; वही यह अब हमें चाहने वाला है। वह वाजों में रक्षक हो, वह बढ़ाने वाला हो और शरीरों का त्राता।
english: May we serve the son of strength, for the giving of oblations; he indeed is now this one desirous of us. May he be the helper in the prizes, may he be the increaser and the protector of bodies.
notes: hināyam is uncertain: read hi + nā + ayam, with nā as a lengthened nu 'now'; possible hi naḥ ayam ('indeed, this one ... us') is also a reading. The '~' in napāta~ is the candrabindu for anusvāra. The god is not named; ūrjo napātam 'son of strength' is the accusative object of dāśema (dāś with the accusative 'serve'). havyadātaye may belong to dāśema, as rendered. ūrj 'strength' (also 'sap, nourishment').

hindi: आओ, हे अग्नि, मैं तुम्हारे लिए इस प्रकार अन्य स्तुतियाँ भली प्रकार कहूँ; इन बूँदों से तुम बढ़ो।
english: Come hither; let me speak to you well, O Agni, thus other songs; with these drops may you grow.
notes: agna is agne (e before i- after the word-final: te agne ittha), and vardhāsa is vardhāse before a vowel (e -> a). itarā giraḥ 'other songs' is object of bravāṇi.

hindi: जहाँ कहीं भी तुम्हारे मन को और उच्चतर कौशल को तुम स्थापित करते हो, वहाँ तुम स्थान बनाते हो।
english: Wherever at all you set your mind and higher skill, there you make a seat.
notes: manaḥ is taken as a second object of dadhase with dakṣam; alternatively 'your mind sets higher skill'. The addressee is not named. tatrā is tatra (lengthened final vowel).

hindi: निश्चय ही तुम्हारी पूर्ति नहीं, हे स्वामी; तब तुम सेवा प्राप्त करते हो।
english: For your fulfilment has not [unclear] [unclear], O lord of [unclear]; then you win service.
notes: akṣipat, bhuvat and nemānām cannot be read with confidence: akṣipat (aor. of kṣip, or a-kṣipat) and nemānām (gen. pl. of an unknown noun, perhaps nema 'some, other') are left as [unclear] and the middle of the sentence is omitted in Hindi. Only 'for your fulfilment', 'O lord' and 'then you win service' are firm.

hindi: हम सहायता चाहने वाले, हे अनुपम, किसी स्थूल खम्भे के समान वहन करते हुए, तुम्हें, हे वज्रधारी, अद्भुत को पुकारते हैं।
english: We indeed, O unequalled one, desiring help, carrying like some stout post, call you, O wielder of the thunderbolt, the wondrous one.
notes: The simile sthūraṃ na kaccit bharantaḥ is obscure; it is kept literal, with no object of 'carrying' supplied. apūrvya 'unequalled' (literally 'without predecessor'). The '~' in vajriñcitra~ is the candrabindu for anusvāra.

hindi: कर्म में सहायता के लिए वह हमारे लिए तुम्हारे पास पहुँचा, तरुण, उग्र, जिसने साहस किया। क्योंकि तुम्हें ही सहायक के रूप में हम मित्रों ने चुना है, हे इन्द्र, विजयी को।
english: He strode up to you for help in the deed, for us, the young, strong one who dared. For we friends have chosen you indeed as helper, O Indra, the winning one.
notes: upa ... cakrāma is read 'strode up to'; the first line is loosely built and the identity of 'he' is not stated. karman = karmann, loc. 'in the deed' (also 'in action'). dhṛṣat is taken as 'boldly/dared'. sakhāyaḥ is a nominative ('we friends'); a vocative 'O friends' is also possible.

hindi: तब हे इन्द्र, हे स्तुतिप्रिय, इच्छा में हम तुम्हारे पास पहुँचते हैं, हमने भेजा है; जल के समान वे जलों के साथ आए।
english: Then indeed, O Indra, O lover of praise, in desire we approach you; we have sent forth. Like water, they came with waters.
notes: sasṛgmahe has no object ('what' is not stated), and the second line (udeva gmanta udabhiḥ) is obscure: gmanta is taken as 3 pl. aorist 'they came'; the line may instead be a comparison for the singers ('going like water with waters'). udeva = udā iva; kāma is kāme before ī-. Kept literal.

hindi: जल के समान, हे शूर, पवित्र वचन तुम्हें धाराओं से बढ़ाते हैं; बढ़े हुए तुम्हें भी, हे पत्थर के धारी, दिन-प्रतिदिन।
english: Like water, the sacred words increase you with streams, O hero; even you who have grown, O wielder of the stone, day by day.
notes: vārṇa = vāḥ na (the ṇ is retroflex after r). yavyābhiḥ is taken as 'with streams' (yavyā); the sense is uncertain. In vavṛdhvā~saṃ the '~' stands for the nasal of vavṛdhvāṃsam. The second line has no verb of its own; 'increase' carries over from line 1.

hindi: वे भूरे दोनों को जोतते हैं, उत्साही के गीत से, चौड़े रथ में, चौड़े जुए वाले में; वाणी से जुते हुए, इन्द्र को वहन करने वाले, प्रकाश पाने वाले।
english: They yoke the two tawny ones with the song of the vigorous one, on the broad chariot with the broad yoke, yoked by speech, carriers of Indra, light-finding.
notes: The three dual adjectives (vacoyujā, indravāhā, svarvidā) describe the two tawny horses. iṣira 'vigorous' (also 'lively, refreshing'); the iṣira is not identified. svar = light of heaven.
